title: Eternal, Spotless Lamb of God
description: Eternal, Spotless Lamb of God in Tonic Solfa to SWEET HOUR, doh is Db: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley wrote these words. John Wesley printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 237.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre Double (8.8.8.8.8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to SWEET HOUR; any other Long Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: E-ter-nal, spot-less Lamb of God, Be-fore the world's_ foun-da-tion slain, Sprin-kle us ev-er with thy blood, O cleanse, and keep_ us ev-er clean! To ev-ery soul (all praise to thee!) Our bow-els of com-pas-sion move; And all man-kind by this may see God is in us_; for God is love.

lines: Eternal, spotless Lamb of God,
Before the world's foundation slain,
Sprinkle us ever with thy blood,
O cleanse, and keep us ever clean!
To every soul (all praise to thee!)
Our bowels of compassion move;
And all mankind by this may see
God is in us; for God is love.
Giver and Lord of life, whose power
And guardian care for all are free,
To thee, in fierce temptation's hour,
From sin and Satan let us flee;
Thine, Lord, we are, and ours thou art,
In us be all thy goodness showed;
Renew, enlarge, and fill our heart
With peace, and joy, and heaven, and God.
Blessing and honour, praise and love,
Co-equal, co-eternal Three,
In earth below, and heaven above,
By all thy works be paid to thee!
Thrice Holy! thine the kingdom is,
The power omnipotent is thine,
And when created nature dies,
Thy never-ceasing glories shine.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to SWEET HOUR by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
